documents.title: Profile — Identity
documents.summary: Pankit Brahmkhatri is a Master's CS student at TU Dresden.

documents.title: Profile — Research focus
documents.summary: His research focuses on agent memory, information retrieval, test-time learning, search-guided reasoning, and reliable tool agents. He builds research prototypes and evaluation systems, and presents their evidence, assumptions, and limitations explicitly.

documents.title: Research overview — Central research question
documents.summary: How can an agent turn remembered or retrieved evidence into a reliable action when sources can be incomplete, stale, conflicting, or wrong? The portfolio approaches this as an end-to-end systems question spanning memory, retrieval, adaptation, reasoning, tools, and evaluation.

documents.title: Research overview — Research method
documents.summary: The projects make evidence boundaries visible, record provenance and time, test interventions or counterfactuals where possible, and distinguish deterministic software checks from broader research claims. They favor calibrated clarification or abstention when the indexed evidence is insufficient.

documents.title: Research overview — Shared system view
documents.summary: The shared framing is memory as a decision system. Across the portfolio, reliable behavior depends on more than storing facts: an agent must recognize relevant evidence, recall it at the right moment, identify its source, decide whether it is still valid, and use it to choose an appropriate action.

documents.title: Research themes — Agent memory and adaptation
documents.summary: This theme studies what an agent should retain, consolidate, correct, or forget. It treats memory as a controlled state that must remain useful across changing contexts rather than as an unbounded transcript.

documents.title: Research themes — Information retrieval and evidence
documents.summary: This theme studies recall, source recollection, provenance, temporal validity, and selective evidence acquisition. The goal is to retrieve evidence that is not merely similar to a query, but relevant, attributable, and timely enough to support a decision.

documents.title: Research themes — Test-time learning
documents.summary: This theme studies safe adaptation during use, including when repeated observations justify parameter promotion and when uncertain evidence should stay outside persistent model state. Adaptation is evaluated as a governed process rather than an automatic update.

documents.title: Research themes — Search-guided reasoning
documents.summary: This theme treats reasoning as a search over hypotheses, evidence requests, and possible actions. Search should expose uncertainty, respect constraints, and stop with clarification or abstention when the available evidence cannot support a reliable choice.

documents.title: Research themes — Reliable tool agents
documents.summary: This theme studies agents that act through tools under concurrency, scope, and failure. Reliability depends on typed state changes, causal influence tests, pre-action verification, and traceable boundaries between observation, decision, and effect.

documents.title: Research connection map — Indexed catalog
documents.summary: The catalog count is generated from the authoritative project records, keeping verified public projects separate from pending title-only entries. The portfolio has 34 indexed project records: 29 verified public projects and 5 pending title-only records.

documents.title: Research connection map — Recognition, recall, source, and action
documents.summary: RKA-Lab connects four evaluation rungs: recognizing remembered evidence, recalling it, identifying its source, and using it to choose an action. The distinction separates fluent answers from memory that causally changes behavior.

documents.title: Research connection map — Concurrency and temporal validity
documents.summary: TxnMem studies concurrent updates to shared agent memory. FreshIndex schedules checks when mutable memories may be stale, while RegimeBank tracks whether experience remains valid after a regime change. Together they connect concurrency control with temporal validity.

documents.title: Research connection map — Consolidation, correction, and forgetting
documents.summary: HippoGate decides whether to retain, probe, consolidate, or forget a candidate memory. MemEquiv tests whether a correction really changes behavior, and CertiCompress asks whether consolidation preserves the constraints that matter.

documents.title: Research connection map — Causal influence, scope, and provenance
documents.summary: MemIntervene measures causal influence by intervening on memory. ScopeGuard limits where learned instructions apply, and CertiCompress preserves provenance through compression. Trace-Mem is connected only at the verified public metadata level; detailed implementation and evaluation claims are intentionally not inferred.

documents.title: Research connection map — Parameter promotion
documents.summary: ParamLedger studies parameter promotion: moving repeated, supported observations into a more persistent state while keeping evidence, timing, and rollback information available for review.

documents.summary: SynthesisAutopsy ![CI](https://github.com/pxnkit/synthesis-autopsy/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![Python 3.12](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3120/) ![License: MIT](LICENSE) Failure-aware evidence search for solid-state oxide synthesis investigations. SynthesisAutopsy is a working research prototype for examining why a solid-state synthesis attempt did not reach its intended phase. It normalizes the attempted procedure, retrieves successful and failed precedents, keeps competing failure hypotheses, compares diagnostic actions, applies deterministic safety rules, and produces a replayable evidence report. The default project runs on CPU with authored synthetic fixtures. It needs no API keys, external services, model downloads, papers, or laboratory datasets. [!IMPORTANT] The bundled records are synthetic and not chemically validated. The software does not diagnose real materials, establish chemical causality, control equipment, or replace expert safety review. documents.title: synthesis-autopsy — ARCHITECTURE.md
documents.summary: Architecture SynthesisAutopsy separates scientific records, deterministic analysis, safety policy, and presentation so each result can be inspected and replayed. ``mermaid flowchart LR A["Case intake"] -- B["Typed normalization"] B -- C["Evidence retrieval"] B -- D["XRD validation"] C -- E["Matched contrasts"] D -- F["Hypothesis ranking"] E -- F F -- G["Action policy"] G -- H["Safety validator"] H -- I["Researcher approval"] I -- J["Observation reveal"] J -- F F -- K["Abstain or report"] B -- L["Provenance ledger"] C -- L F -- L G -- L J -- L ` Runtime surfaces The Python package is the reference implementation for the API, command line workflow, fixture benchmark, replay, and report generation. The hosted web application provides a credential free interactive workbench using the same versioned fixture concepts and safety vocabulary. The default profile runs on CPU and does not contact external services. Optional scientific libraries and data adapters are isolated from the fixture path. Analysis contract Every analysis returns: - normalized case fields with raw provenance - retrieved successful and failed precedents - matched contrasts with declared variable differences - ranked heuristic hypotheses with supporting and contradicting evidence - missing discriminators - validated diagnostic actions with cost, time, sample, and risk estimates - an abstention decision when evidence is insufficient - a chained audit record for replay The system uses the word score for heuristic rankings. It reserves probability` for future models that pass calibration evaluation.

documents.summary: ChaffMem Lab ChaffMem Lab studies memory availability in bounded agent systems. It asks whether one important and true memory remains stored, retrievable, and useful after the system receives many individually harmless records near the same topic. This repository is a working research prototype. It includes a deterministic Python engine, a local API, a command line interface, a live browser application, replayable traces, controlled comparison arms, tests, and generated smoke-study artifacts. It does not establish that any commercial system is vulnerable. It does not claim a new state of the art result. Full cross-domain benchmarks and statistical conclusions remain open research work. Retrieval availability asks whether it appears inside a fixed top-k result 3. Behavioral availability asks whether a downstream decision uses it 4. documents.summary: boundary This repository is for defensive research on local memory implementations. - Do not connect it to a hosted assistant for adversarial testing - Do not add prompt injection, executable payloads, credential access, persistence, or evasion - Keep traffic inside disposable local stores - Use only benign and auditable fixture records - Treat alerts as research signals, not proof of an attack - Do not infer a product vulnerability from this simulator See SECURITY.md and paper/ethics.md for reporting and responsible-use guidance. Known limitations The default embedding is intentionally lightweight. It supports reproducible CPU studies but does not represent the geometry of a learned production retriever. The live browser engine mirrors the study concepts but is not the source of publication evidence. Smoke runs are too small for a broad statistical conclusion. The symbolic behavior task isolates causal use of a memory but does not model every failure mode of an LLM agent. Originality and provenance The repository contains an independent implementation written for this project. No third-party source code, experiment output, prose, figure, dataset, or model weight is bundled. Broad research concepts such as bounded storage, retrieval ranking, quotas, replay, and canary monitoring are implemented through project-specific interfaces and deterministic fixtures. Any future integration that incorporates a third-party method, dataset, model, or codebase must add its license and scholarly attribution before release. documents.summary: Architecture ChaffMem Lab separates experiment control, memory behavior, traffic generation, defenses, evaluation, and presentation. Each boundary is typed and traceable. Runtime surfaces Python research engine The Python package is authoritative for benchmark execution and artifacts. It owns: - Typed configuration and domain records - Deterministic embeddings - Fixed-capacity memory policies - Benign traffic and attack selection - Defense decisions - Canary evaluation - Symbolic downstream actions - Metrics and report generation - Snapshot, replay, and audit - FastAPI and CLI adapters Browser reference engine The live application contains a compact deterministic implementation for interactive exploration. It has no external dependency and stores no server-side data. Browser output illustrates the method but is not used as publication evidence. Deployment worker The web build targets a Cloudflare-compatible worker. It serves the React application and static assets. No research database, identity flow, or secret is required for the public demo. Experiment lifecycle 1. Validate and normalize a versioned configuration 2. Create a deterministic run identifier 3. Seed the critical and ordinary records 4. Select a benign candidate under the declared knowledge condition 5. Apply write-time defense admission 6. Write the record and enforce fixed capacity 7. Query the target and ordinary utility tasks 8. Execute the symbolic downstream action 9. Append hash-chained decisions and metrics 10. Repeat until the write budget is exhausted 11. Write the immutable manifest, verify

documents.title: paramledger — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: ParamLedger ParamLedger is an executable research system for evidence-governed parametric memory. It treats an adapter as a compiled view of an authoritative experience ledger. Repeated evidence can promote into a small immutable update only after support, utility, locality, interaction, privacy, and cost checks pass. Later contradictions can quarantine or replace that update through a measured rollback transaction. The default path runs on CPU without an API key, GPU, proprietary model, external database, or network access after dependencies are installed. What works The repository provides a complete, deterministic vertical slice. - An append-only SQLite event ledger with schema versions and a SHA-256 hash chain. - An encrypted payload store with one key per record and hard erasure. - Deterministic materialized views and a queryable lineage graph. - Typed memories for facts, intent rules, procedures, tool schemas, preferences, and safety constraints. - Shared-cause support clustering that collapses mirrored evidence. - A multi-gate promotion policy with calibrated risk input. - Real rank-2 adapter training for a frozen CPU model. - Immutable manifests with base, tokenizer, transformation, and artifact hashes. - Safe NPZ loading with pickle disabled. - Optional PyTorch low-rank and Hugging Face PEFT backends. - Pre-output routing with scope, validity, conflict, dependency, and budget checks. - Controlled-direct behavioral interventions. - Structured root-cause attribution. - Optimistic activation epochs and atomic pointer replacement. - Rollback previews, post-change

documents.title: rka-lab — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: RKA-Lab RKA-Lab is an evaluation library for a narrow question in agent memory research: Does a remembered fact survive the path from recognition to recall, source recollection, and correct action? The library evaluates all four rungs against the same evidence. Every item also runs with a matched irrelevant-memory mask and a gold-memory mask. This makes it possible to distinguish fluent answers from evidence-linked memory that changes behavior. RKA-Lab is an end-to-end software prototype. It includes a typed Python library, offline baselines, a command-line interface, a FastAPI service, a React research workbench, deterministic tool environments, Docker, CI, tests, and publication artifacts. The included 10-item snapshot is an original deterministic fixture for software verification. It is not the planned 300 to 500 item RKABench research release. No benchmark result in this repository establishes the research hypothesis or publication readiness. What RKA-Lab measures Each evidence-linked item produces four matched tests. | Rung | Test | Failure exposed | | --- | --- | --- | | Recognition | Choose among controlled alternatives | Lucky guessing and weak discrimination | | Recall | Produce the fact without choices | Choice support that does not survive free recall | | Source | Locate the exact session, turn, image, and region | Correct text without evidence recollection | | Action | Execute a replayable tool call | Correct language that does not become correct behavior | Every rung runs under three intervention arms. | Arm | Change | Expected use | | --- | --- | --- | |

documents.title: rka-lab — docs/benchmark_protocol.md - part 1
documents.summary: RKABench protocol Scope RKABench is the planned 300 to 500 item evidence-linked benchmark release for RKA-Lab. The repository currently includes a 10-item deterministic smoke fixture only. Release status: NOT YET TESTED Unit of analysis The unit is an item derived from a base evidence group. All derived questions and interventions from the same base evidence stay in one split. Each item must include: 1. controlled-alternative recognition 2. free recall 3. exact session, turn, image, and region recollection when applicable 4. a replayable task action 5. a matched irrelevant-memory intervention 6. deletion or masking of every declared sufficient gold memory Required coverage The release targets: - corrections - temporal updates - multi-session reasoning - ambiguous recognition foils - unanswerable items - correct text paired with an incorrect tool action - multiple sufficient memories - redundant evidence - image-region evidence - semantically equivalent actions - tool failures unrelated to memory - judge disagreement Split policy Splits are assigned by base evidence id before question variants are generated. Recommended proportions: - train: 20 percent for adapter development - validation: 20 percent for thresholds and prompt selection - test: 60 percent held out for final evaluation No result may be reported if a base evidence group appears in more than one split. Human review Every release item requires: - one evidence and source verification - one foil and leakage review - one action replay - a second review for image-region items and judge-disagreement items

documents.title: txnmem — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: TxnMem TxnMem is a transactional shared-memory service for concurrent agent teams. It gives facts, constraints, resources, commitments, evidence, and commutative values explicit update semantics. Every accepted history can be replayed from an append-only event log and checked against a deterministic serial interpreter. The repository includes the service, the MemoryRace concurrency benchmark, eleven baseline configurations, fault injection, an authenticated API, a command line interface, a PostgreSQL adapter, a bounded semantic-serializability checker, and an interactive trace lab. This is a research prototype. It makes no claim of novelty, priority, or production readiness. A complete literature review and an independent replication are required before using the artifacts in a publication. Why this exists Agent memory is often treated as a text retrieval problem. Shared memory changes the failure model. Two individually reasonable updates can lose information, overbook a resource, revive a retracted claim, or complete a dependent task too early. TxnMem makes those transitions explicit: 1. An agent begins from a versioned snapshot 2. Reads capture record revisions 3. Typed operations are staged without changing canonical state 4. Local preconditions are checked 5. Noncommutative stale reads are classified as conflicts 6. Only declared commutative values merge automatically 7. Global invariants run inside the atomic commit boundary 8. The state update and event records commit together 9. Unsafe rebases remain proposals until an authorized principal approves them What is

documents.title: txnmem — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture TxnMem separates canonical state transitions from agent reasoning. Agents can propose operations and explain conflicts, but deterministic code decides whether state changes. Components Typed protocol models.py defines a discriminated union for every mutation. The union rejects extra fields and validates revision, capacity, idempotency, scope, and vector-clock data before an operation reaches storage. Reference interpreter domain.py is a pure serial interpreter. It applies operations to an immutable copy of the input state and returns a new state or a structured failure. The checker and benchmark reuse the same interpreter. Transaction engine engine.py implements snapshot begin, versioned reads, staging, validation, optimistic commit, conflict classification, idempotent replay, and abort. Disjoint keys can commit from stale snapshots when every declared read remains unchanged. Noncommutative stale reads return a conflict. Only MergeCommutativeValue bypasses same-key stale detection. Invariant gate constraints.py validates built-in resource, commitment, evidence, and executable policy constraints. The final gate runs before the canonical state update inside the same storage transaction. Storage SQLite provides deterministic local execution with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, full synchronous durability, compare-and-swap version updates, and an append-only event log. PostgreSQL uses SELECT FOR UPDATE, a conditional state update, JSONB events, and one transaction for canonical state, events, transaction status, and audit entries. Checker The bounded checker enumerates legal

MemoryRace The benchmark produces typed initial state, agent programs, seeds, interleavings, outcomes, and checker results. Baselines consume the same task definitions. Trace lab The web interface is an interactive protocol model. It visualizes representative traces and makes the safety difference between key conflicts and semantic conflicts concrete. Python artifacts remain authoritative. Commit sequence ``mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Agent participant E as Transaction engine participant V as Invariant gate participant S as Event store A- E: Begin from snapshot A- E: Read typed keys A- E: Stage typed operations E- E: Check revisions and idempotency E- V: Validate projected state V-- E: Valid or structured failure E- S: Compare and swap state version S-- E: Commit state, events, and audit atomically E-- A: Commit result or conflict certificate `` Trust boundary The trusted computing base includes operation schemas, authorization policies, the reference interpreter, invariant validators, the transaction engine, and the storage adapter. Agent prompts, memory text, model output, benchmark descriptions, imported evidence, and UI input are untrusted data.

documents.title: txnmem — docs/consistency.md - part 1
documents.summary: Consistency contract Provided guarantee TxnMem provides snapshot reads and optimistic serializable commits over declared dependencies in a single-primary database. A successful transaction has one atomic position in the canonical event history. Its state update, operation events, transaction status, and audit decision become visible together. For bounded histories, the checker can return a legal serial witness whose semantic projection matches the observed state. If no order matches, it returns a violation certificate. Semantic equivalence Semantic equivalence compares: - Active and retracted facts - Executable constraints - Resource capacities and reservations - Commitment status and dependencies - Evidence activity and claim links - Commutative totals and members Storage metadata such as timestamps and event identifiers does not determine semantic equivalence. Opacity and aborted work Reads come from the transaction snapshot. Staged and aborted writes never appear in canonical state. The current implementation does not expose staged state to another transaction. Conflict scope The guarantee depends on complete typed dependencies. Built-in operations derive their canonical target. Cross-key reasoning dependencies must be captured by a typed read or an executable invariant. An application that omits a relevant read and has no validator can still admit write skew. This is a protocol misuse, not a hidden guarantee. Failure tolerance Supported: - Duplicate delivery with the same logical idempotency key - Retry after an unknown commit acknowledgement - Process crash before a

documents.summary: database commit - Process crash after commit and before response - Stale snapshots - Delay and reordering - Malformed or unauthorized operations - Model timeout during optional rebase generation Not claimed: - Multi-primary linearizability - Progress during a database partition - Byzantine database or principal behavior - Clock-based ordering without vector or revision evidence - Exactly-once external side effects outside the database Storage notes SQLite uses one local writer and is intended for deterministic experiments, tests, and small deployments. PostgreSQL uses a locked canonical-state row and is the production reference adapter. Its current implementation is single primary. External failover behavior must be tested against the chosen database service.

documents.title: txnmem — docs/protocol.md - part 1
documents.summary: Transaction protocol Operation envelope Every operation carries: - Operation and transaction identifiers - Principal and task scope - Snapshot base version - Target and operation-specific payload - Expected record revision where required - Vector clock - Idempotency key - Timestamp The target namespace is derived from the operation type. Clients cannot provide arbitrary read or write sets that disagree with the typed target. Lifecycle Begin begin reads the current canonical state and stores the full snapshot with an open transaction record. Read read returns values from the stored snapshot. Each key is added to the transaction read set with its record version. Stage stage validates the discriminated operation schema, principal, task scope, transaction identifier, and base version. Staging does not change canonical state. Validate validate runs the serial interpreter against the original snapshot. It is an early deterministic check and does not reserve a commit version. Commit Commit loads current state and performs these checks: 1. Match idempotency keys to logical operation fingerprints 2. Compare every declared read and noncommutative write with the snapshot record version 3. Reapply operations over current canonical state 4. Run global invariants on the projected state 5. Compare and swap the canonical state version 6. Append operation events and the audit decision 7. Mark the transaction committed Steps five through seven run in one database transaction. Conflict A conflict record contains its type, code, affected operations, keys, constraints, message, and retry status.

documents.title: txnmem — docs/protocol.md - part 2
documents.summary: Syntactic conflicts include stale revisions, reused identifiers, duplicate completions, and incompatible idempotency reuse. Semantic conflicts include resource over-allocation, inactive evidence dependencies, commitment order failures, and executable constraint violations. Rebase Rebase candidates are deterministic and operation specific. A candidate is validated before it is returned. Nontrivial candidates require an approval credential and commit as a new transaction. TxnMem never merges arbitrary text into canonical state. Abort Abort records the reason and closes the transaction without changing canonical state. Idempotency The fingerprint excludes transport-specific identifiers, timestamps, base versions, and vector clocks. It includes the principal, scope, operation type, target, and semantic payload. Retrying the same logical operation with the same key returns replayed and does not duplicate the effect. Reusing the key for a different logical operation returns an idempotency conflict. Commutativity MergeCommutativeValue combines a numeric delta and a grow-only member set. Property tests verify order independence. No other operation is treated as commutative. New commutative declarations require an algebraic argument and exhaustive property tests.

documents.title: chronicle-guard — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: ChronicleGuard ChronicleGuard is a source-aware evaluation platform for multimodal agent recall. It measures whether language received after a visual event changes an agent's later answer about the original observation. The system keeps raw episodic evidence separate from mutable current-world beliefs. A routing gate records reports, corrections, updates, and unsupported suggestions without rewriting the original event. This repository ships a complete CPU-only path with synthetic visual scenes, a FastAPI service, a browser workbench, deterministic baselines, paired causal analysis, and reproducible run artifacts. External vision-language models are optional. What works - A live timeline workbench for adding accurate, misleading, irrelevant, correcting, and updating statements - Immutable episodic records with a digest that is verified after every write - A bi-temporal belief timeline for legitimate changes to the world - Full-context, last-write-wins, dual-store, and oracle routing baselines - A 60-sequence offline fixture with ten original synthetic scenes - A configurable generator for larger paired benchmarks - Exact scoring, calibration, clustered bootstrap intervals, and randomization inference - A versioned FastAPI contract and command-line workflow - Unit, property, metamorphic, integrity, API, statistical, and rendered-site tests - Exportable episode traces with evidence regions and routing decisions The bundled fixture is a software validation suite. Its deterministic effects are not scientific findings. Research contract The primary estimand is: ``text

documents.title: chronicle-guard — README.md - part 2
documents.summary: P(original-event error | misleading report) - P(original-event error | neutral report) ` Treatments are paired within each base visual scene. Uncertainty is clustered by base scene so paraphrases and treatment variants are not treated as independent observations. ChronicleGuard asks three separate questions: 1. What was present in the original event 2. What is true in the current world state 3. Which evidence supports the answer The separation is deliberate. A later update may change the current answer without changing what the original image contained. Architecture `mermaid flowchart LR A["Synthetic visual event"] -- B["Immutable episodic store"] C["Post-event statement"] -- D["Reconsolidation gate"] D -- E["Report ledger"] D -- F["Belief timeline"] D -- G["Quarantine"] H["Probe intent"] -- I{"Original, current, or source"} I -- B I -- F B -- J["Answer with provenance"] F -- J E -- J ` Store A contains the event image digest, observation timestamp, structured claim, uncertainty, and evidence region. It is append-only. Store B contains versioned beliefs with valid time, transaction time, source, confidence, and supersession links. The gate never acts as a truth authority. It decides where a statement belongs and preserves competing accounts when evidence is weak. documents.summary: Architecture Design goals ChronicleGuard is built around four guarantees: 1. Original evidence is append-only and digest verified 2. Later reports cannot silently become observations 3. Legitimate world changes remain representable 4. documents.summary: Benchmark card Name ChronicleGuard Controlled Recall Fixture Purpose The fixture tests whether the benchmark, storage, routing, probing, and statistical pipelines behave as specified before external models are used. It is not a leaderboard and its deterministic results are not evidence of model behavior. Composition - 10 synthetic base scenes - 6 matched treatment histories per scene - 60 sequences - 3 probes per sequence - 180 question instances - 100 percent generated visual content - No people or sensitive scenes The six conditions are neutral, accurate, misleading, misleading with correction, legitimate update, and misleading with legitimate update. Abilities The scenes cover: - Object attribute recall - Spatial relation recall - Counting - Text and symbol reading - Current-state updating - Evidence localization - Source monitoring - Abstention and quarantine behavior Construction Pillow renders each scene from fixed primitives. Image bytes are hashed before the event is sealed. Statements are generated from controlled templates and carry a treatment label that is never exposed to model adapters. Larger runs repeat the factorial cells with new seeds and surface variants. Splits Non-fixture runs assign splits by a stable hash of base item id. Every treatment, paraphrase, and probe derived from one base scene remains in the same split. assert no split leakage rejects a build when this invariant fails. Schemas Each sequence includes: - A VisualEpisode - An immutable EpisodicRecord - One or more PostEventStatement records - Original-event, current-state, and source probes - Controlled factor labels - A base scene ID and split Integrity Each PNG has a SHA-256 digest. The digest is stored in the episode and included in the canonical episodic payload. The benchmark manifest stores a digest over all serialized sequences. Quality checks - Unique sequence IDs - Stable scene digests - Base-scene split isolation - Balanced fixture conditions - Gold-answer isolation - Schema validation - Round-trip serialization - Original-evidence integrity after arbitrary text Maintenance Changes to a scene, treatment template, or schema require a version increment and a new dataset digest.

documents.title: chronicle-guard — docs/evaluation.md
documents.summary: Evaluation protocol Primary outcome Original-event error is one when the response does not match the observation-time gold answer. The primary misinformation effect is the error-rate difference between misleading and neutral treatment within the same base scene. Secondary outcomes - Current-state accuracy - Source localization - Correction recovery - Legitimate-update retention - Confidence-weighted error - Brier score - Evidence-region citation - Abstention - Latency and cost Pairing Neutral and treated sequences share the base scene, visual claim, and probe. Surface forms and order may vary, but the target event remains fixed. Dependence Treatment variants from one base scene are dependent. ChronicleGuard clusters bootstrap resampling by base item id. Randomization inference The paired randomization test swaps neutral and misleading labels within base scenes. The reported p-value uses a plus-one correction. Calibration Brier score is computed as: ``text (reported confidence - correctness)^2 `` Calibration must be reported beside accuracy because an incorrect high-confidence answer is a distinct failure. Manual review Exact evaluation is the default. If external model output is ambiguous: 1. Remove model and treatment identifiers 2. Present the response and allowed gold set to reviewers 3. Require a recorded rationale 4. Report agreement and adjudication 5. Re-run headline results under strict exact scoring Reporting Do not collapse model-family null results into one average. Include per-model effects, intervals, treatment counts, failed responses, and missing runs.

All systems must receive equivalent: - Image access - Treatment history - Token budget - Retrieval budget - Probe wording Limitations Provider behavior can change without a model-name change. Archive model revisions, prompts, request parameters, and raw responses with every run.

documents.title: intentledger — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: IntentLedger IntentLedger is a cancellation-safe prospective memory runtime for long-horizon agents. It keeps future intentions in an append-only event ledger and rechecks lifecycle state, trigger evidence, preconditions, version, and idempotency immediately before execution. The repository includes a deterministic Python core, FastAPI service, command line interface, interactive simulated week, synthetic lifecycle benchmark, baseline suite, research artifacts, and a deployable web workbench. This is an independent implementation. The repository contains no third-party paper, benchmark archive, copied source code, external dataset, or reproduced result. Why this exists Long-running agents need to remember more than what to do. They must also know when an instruction is no longer valid. A reminder can become unsafe after it is cancelled, amended, completed elsewhere, suspended, expired, or replaced. IntentLedger treats these changes as first-class events. The current intention is a projection of immutable history, not a mutable note that silently loses context. The runtime follows one rule: ``text active and trigger is true and preconditions are true and time is valid and this version is current and this instance has not executed ` If any condition fails, the runtime returns a structured suppression reason. What is included | Area | Implementation | | --- | --- | | Lifecycle | Draft, active, suspended, completed, cancelled, expired, invalidated, and superseded states | | Event store | SQLite append-only log with per-stream sequence numbers, idempotency keys, and SHA-256 hash

documents.summary: Architecture Design goals IntentLedger is built around four properties: 1. Lifecycle changes are immutable facts 2. Current state is reproducible from the event log 3. Parser and model output cannot bypass deterministic guards 4. Execution is idempotent and bound to one intention version Components Domain model src/intentledger/models.py defines typed intentions, triggers, preconditions, actions, ledger events, proposals, projections, and decisions with Pydantic v2. The domain has no dependency on FastAPI, SQLite, or a model provider. State machine src/intentledger/state machine.py contains the permitted lifecycle transitions. Terminal states have no outgoing transitions. An amendment changes the version but preserves the current nonterminal lifecycle state. Event store src/intentledger/store.py writes events to SQLite in an immediate transaction. Each stream has: - A strictly increasing sequence number - A unique idempotency key - A previous event hash - A SHA-256 event hash over canonical JSON - Event time and processing time - Actor, correlation, and causation metadata The event log is the source of truth. Projections are disposable. Projection engine src/intentledger/engine.py rebuilds an intention from sequence one. It does not trust a cached current state. The engine owns: - Create and amendment semantics - Lifecycle commands - Environment observations - Virtual clock advancement - Proposal creation - Approval - Final execution rechecks - Export and invariant verification Monitors src/intentledger/monitor.py evaluates exact time, windows, typed events, state

The browser workbench under app/ is a credential-free interactive demonstration. It mirrors the safety model and performs sandbox simulations only. Ordering Events that share an event timestamp are ordered by semantic precedence: 1. Cancellation 2. Amendment 3. Suspension 4. Completion 5. Invalidation 6. Reactivation 7. Trigger observation 8. Precondition change Processing time breaks ties after semantic precedence. This ordering ensures a cancellation at the trigger timestamp prevents a proposal. Consistency model SQLite serializes appends with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Idempotency is enforced by a unique database constraint. The reference runtime provides single-database consistency. Distributed adapters must preserve stream sequence, idempotency, and lifecycle precedence. Hidden future events are excluded. Eligibility An intention is eligible for recurrence instance k when: ``text Eligible(I, k, t) = S(I, t) = active and T(I, Ht) and P(I, Ht) and W(I, t) and V(I, t) is current and not D(I, k) and every dependency is completed and execution count(I) < max executions(I) ` An eligible decision permits proposal creation. It does not permit execution. Execution `text Execute(I, proposal, t) = Eligible(I, proposal.instance, t) and proposal.version = V(I, t) and proposal.expires at = t and approval required(I) implies A(I, t) ` Execution appends one ActionExecuted event with an idempotency key derived from the proposal and recurrence instance. Small-step transitions The transition relation has the form: `text projection, event - projection' ` Creation: `text empty, IntentCreated(spec, v=1, state) - Projection(spec, v=1, state) ` Amendment: `text Projection(spec, v, nonterminal), IntentAmended(spec', v+1) - Projection(spec', v+1, same state) ` Lifecycle: `text Projection(spec, v, active), IntentCancelled - Projection(spec, v, cancelled) ` Proposal: `text

Cancellation therefore wins over triggering. The implementation sorts by: `text event time, semantic precedence, idempotency key ` Late and out-of-order events Event time records when a fact occurred. Processing time records when the runtime observed it. The append-only sequence follows processing order. A late event does not rewrite earlier state. Evaluation applies the full visible history with explicit precedence. Production distributed adapters should define a bounded lateness policy and watermark. The reference runtime keeps all late events and exposes their timestamps for analysis. Recurrence identity Time recurrence: `text instance key = intention id + version + localized target time ` Typed or semantic event recurrence: `text instance key = observation id `` Changing the intention creates a new version and therefore a new instance namespace. Invariants 1. Terminal state never proposes or executes 2. One recurrence instance executes at most once 3. Approval for one version cannot authorize another 4. Invalid lifecycle transitions are rejected 5. Replay from sequence one equals the current projection 6. Every event hash matches its canonical envelope 7. Every previous hash matches the prior event 8.

documents.summary: WhoFixesThis WhoFixesThis is an offline-first research prototype for evidence-based civic service routing. It takes an issue description, location context, observation time, uncertainty, and an optional asset identifier. It then constructs competing provider and service hypotheses, searches dated evidence, checks likely duplicates, and either selects a supported route or abstains. It is not government guidance and it never submits a report. documents.title: freshindex — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: FreshIndex FreshIndex schedules proactive verification for mutable agent memory when audit capacity is limited. It assigns each memory an age-aware priority, explains the score, dispatches only allowlisted verifiers, and records every decision in a tamper-evident event log. Live dashboard | API reference | Research scope The repository is a working research prototype. It includes a FastAPI service, a deterministic simulator, conservative posterior policies, exact small-state validation, symbolic checks, a React dashboard, paper artifacts, and automated tests. Why this exists Long-running agents store facts that can change outside the agent. Verification reduces the risk of using stale memory, but checking every item on every round is rarely practical. A useful scheduler has to decide which few items deserve attention now. FreshIndex models an item's verification age as the state of a restless arm. For the base model, the stale probability after age \(a\) is \[ q(a) = 1 - (1 - h)^a \] where \(h\) is the per-period change hazard. If the item is used with probability \(\lambda\) and a stale use incurs loss \(L\), its expected one-period stale-use cost is \[ c(a) = \lambda L q(a) \] The renewal comparison between auditing at age \(a\) and waiting one more period gives the break-even activation charge \[ W(a) = (a + 1)c(a + 1) - \sum {s=0}^{a} c(s) \] For nondecreasing \(c(a)\), adjacent scores satisfy \[ W(a + 1) - W(a) = (a + 2)[c(a + 2) - c(a + 1)] \ge 0 \] This monotonicity gives the single-item threshold and indexability result under the assumptions stated in the theorem

The ranked policy is a transparent projection back to a per-round capacity limit. Inconclusive and error outcomes remain in the evidence log but do not reset age. A second concurrent audit for the same memory is rejected. Useful read endpoints: | Endpoint | Purpose | | --- | --- | | GET /health | Service and event-chain health | | GET /v1/items | Fleet state and current beliefs | | GET /v1/events | Ordered append-only events | | GET /v1/replay | State rebuilt from the event stream | | GET /v1/export | Portable research snapshot | | POST /v1/policies/compare | Counterfactual schedules on one state | Scheduler conventions FreshIndex uses an activation-charge convention. The base index is the total charge at which auditing now and waiting one more age step have equal renewal cost. If an item has audit cost \(v i\), its selection priority is \[ I i(a) = W i(a) - v i \] A round selects at most \(B\) items with positive priority. Exact ties are ordered by age and stable item identifier. The full tie groups remain in ScheduleDecision, which makes replay independent of process ordering. Boundary behavior is intentional: - \(h = 0\), \(\lambda = 0\), or \(L = 0\) gives a zero index - \(h = 1\) is handled without numerical cancellation - \(B = 0\) selects nothing - \(B \ge N\) still skips nonpositive adjusted scores because capacity is an upper bound - Empty and fully retired fleets return an empty schedule - Ages saturate at the configured cap - At the cap, cost is treated as saturated and the score compares auditing with remaining at the cap

documents.summary: Learning policy Verification at age \(a\) reveals whether at least one change occurred, not the exact change time. This feedback is interval-censored. The current hazard learner uses a conservative Beta approximation: - A fresh outcome contributes \(a\) observed no-change periods - A stale outcome contributes one change and no assumed pre-change exposure - The conservative policy ranks with upper uncertainty bounds - Thompson policy samples from the current approximate posterior This update is labeled EMPIRICAL ONLY in the theorem ledger. It is not a conjugate posterior for censored change time and no regret theorem is claimed. The benchmark package tests its calibration and failure modes. Usage uses a Gamma-Poisson exposure model. Loss is supplied by the application and may be paired with external uncertainty analysis. A production deployment should connect loss values to a governed risk taxonomy. Verification safety Verifiers are registered as typed adapters. A request can select an adapter by name, but it cannot provide code, an import path, or a shell command. Every accepted result must satisfy all of these checks: - The action exists and is still current - The action and result refer to the same memory - The evidence hash matches canonical JSON - The signature matches the adapter secret - Status-specific fields are present - No completed action is accepted twice The bundled HMAC signer is suitable for a local prototype. A production system should use an external key manager and asymmetric signatures so verifiers do not share signing material with the scheduler.

Run the full validation suite: `bash pytest ruff check . mypy freshindex cd ui npm test npm run build ` The continuous integration workflow runs the same checks on Python 3.11 and 3.12. It also compares formula behavior with renewal calculations and exact small-state dynamic programming. Research artifacts are organized as follows: `text theory/ proofs/ Human-readable proofs theorem status.md Claim and proof-status ledger notation.md Symbols and conventions counterexamples.md Known failures outside the base model paper/ claims/ Claims and evidence mapping results/ Machine-readable experiment summaries related work.bib Scholarly references reproducibility.md Artifact checklist configs/ smoke.yaml Deterministic acceptance run sources.yaml Source and license registry `` Research status The base single-item threshold and indexability claims are proved for nondecreasing age cost with perfect, immediate reset. Symbolic identities and exhaustive numerical checks back the derivation. They do not replace the stated proof. The following features are empirical: - Unknown hazard learning from censored outcomes - Conservative uncertainty bonuses - Hard-capacity multi-item ranking - Imperfect audits - Delayed results - Correlated changes - Abrupt hazard shifts Results from these tracks must be described as measurements.

documents.summary: The project does not call an empirical pattern a proof. Source and attribution policy This repository contains original code, prose, tests, and figures. It does not contain third-party paper files or copied research implementations. Established concepts are cited in the source registry and paper bibliography. Citation is used to separate prior work from this prototype's contribution, not to claim another author's work. See docs/source registry.md for versions, licenses, intended use, and checksums. The static dashboard is a client-side demonstration. It does not persist data or execute the Python verifier service. documents.title: freshindex — docs/research_scope.md - part 1
documents.summary: Research scope Research question Can a transparent age-based audit index reduce stale-use loss under limited verification capacity, relative to fixed TTL and immediate-risk scheduling, without hiding model failure? Base model The proof package assumes: - Independent memory items - Discrete rounds - Observable verification age - Constant per-period geometric change hazard - Independent usage - Fixed stale-use loss - Perfect audit - Immediate reset - Nondecreasing age cost - Average-cost objective These assumptions produce a renewal cycle and a closed-form break-even audit charge. System contribution FreshIndex connects the analytical score to an auditable service. It records the parameters used for each decision, exposes score decomposition, isolates verifiers behind typed adapters, distinguishes all audit outcomes, and supports deterministic replay. Novelty boundary The project does not claim to invent restless bandits, Whittle indices, posterior sampling, or agent memory. Its contribution is the specified age-cost model, the implementation discipline around proactive memory verification, and the linked theory-to-test artifact. The hard-capacity ranking policy and conservative censored-feedback learner are evaluated algorithms. They are not covered by the base theorem. Falsification criteria The research claim should be narrowed or withdrawn if any of these preregistered checks fail: - The formula disagrees with adjacent renewal-cost indifference - The index decreases under a cost sequence that satisfies the base assumptions - Immediate-risk scheduling matches the index

documents.title: hippogate — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: HippoGate HippoGate is a research system for deciding what an adaptive agent should do with a candidate memory. It can forget the candidate, keep it episodically, run a targeted cross-context probe, or consolidate it into semantic memory. The controller treats cross-context applicability as a hidden binary state. It maintains a calibrated posterior belief and solves a discounted belief-state decision problem. This makes the consolidation rule inspectable. Every decision can be traced to the posterior, cost model, horizon, recurrence estimate, and probe likelihoods that produced it. The repository includes the mathematical core, finite and infinite-horizon solvers, direct enumeration checks, synthetic and procedural environments, baseline policies, an API, a command-line interface, and an interactive phase diagram. Live phase diagram: pxnkit.github.io/hippogate Why this project exists Memory systems often use rules such as "store after two successful uses" or "keep anything above a confidence threshold." Those rules ignore the cost of a wrong generalization, the value of another observation, the probability that a memory will recur, and the quality of the available validation context. HippoGate asks a narrower and testable question: Given current evidence and explicit costs, which memory action has the highest expected value? This framing is useful when an experience may be valid in one context but unsafe in another. Examples include retry procedures, schema mappings, tool-use workflows, API conventions, and learned task strategies. HippoGate does not update model weights in

documents.title: hippogate — README.md - part 2
documents.summary: its default path. Consolidation creates an explicit, versioned semantic rule with scope, evidence, posterior, validation contexts, provenance, and rollback metadata. Parameter updates can be added as a separate adapter without changing the core decision problem. Decision model For one candidate rule, let the hidden applicability state be ``text z = 0 context-specific z = 1 reusable ` The controller never observes z. It maintains `text p t = P(z = 1 | evidence through time t) ` A probe produces an outcome under a context-dependent likelihood model. For an observed outcome y, the exact Bayesian update is `text p P(y | z = 1) p' = ------------------------------- p P(y | z = 1) + (1-p) P(y | z = 0) ` The implementation evaluates four actions: | Action | Meaning | | --- | --- | | forget | Stop tracking the candidate and accept possible missed value | | episodic | Keep the candidate without generalizing it and pay a retention cost | | probe | Validate the candidate in another context and update the posterior | | consolidate | Store a scoped semantic rule and accept possible interference | Terminal values are linear in the belief. Probe and episodic values include discounted continuation value. The solver computes the Bellman maximum over every available action. The default reward model exposes: - reusable semantic value - harmful interference cost - consolidation cost - missed useful consolidation cost - episodic storage cost - recurrence probability - probe cost - discount No cost is hidden inside a learned score. What is implemented Mathematical core - log-odds Bayesian updates

documents.summary: It does not claim an exact continuous-belief solution. Use hippogate.solvers.diagnostics.compare grids to measure the maximum value difference and action agreement between two grid resolutions. The API returns this report for every finite-horizon solve. The default benchmark uses synthetic and deterministic procedural tasks. Performance on these tasks does not establish general agent-memory improvements. documents.title: hypothesisops — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: HypothesisOps HypothesisOps is a research platform for safe, sequential cloud incident diagnosis. It keeps several causal explanations alive, predicts what each explanation implies, and selects a bounded observation or sandbox intervention that can separate them. The first release proves the complete loop in a deterministic simulator. It includes paired ambiguous incidents, typed actions, a fail-closed safety policy, value-of-information search, baseline policies, replay notebooks, statistical summaries, an HTTP API, a CLI, a small container testbed, and a live investigation workbench. The system does not connect to production services. It cannot execute model-generated shell commands. A regional timeout policy can resemble packet loss. HypothesisOps treats the next observation as a decision: ``mermaid flowchart LR A["Ambiguous symptom"] -- B["Competing causal hypotheses"] B -- C["Predict probe outcomes"] C -- D["Safety and budget gate"] D -- E["Run one bounded probe"] E -- F["Update belief state"] F -- G{"Verified or confident"} G -- |No| C G -- |Yes| H["Diagnosis, audit, and replay"] ` The controller scores expected information and decision improvement against telemetry volume, elapsed time, risk, and disruption. Every requested action passes through the safety policy before execution. Live workbench The Incident Investigation Workbench is a complete browser implementation of the research loop. It supports: - Switching between paired ambiguous incidents - Inspecting topology, symptoms, and causal chains - Comparing live hypothesis scores - Selecting safe probes with predicted gain and cost - Updating belief state from deterministic observations - Recording allowed and blocked actions - Verifying a recovery in a digital twin - Exporting a replayable JSON notebook - Reviewing executed smoke benchmark results The browser demo uses deterministic local fixtures. The Python controller implements the same system boundary for experiments and API use. documents.title: methodchain — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: MethodChain MethodChain reconstructs experimental procedures whose parameters are distributed across cited methods and supporting files. The system returns a typed protocol, a document search trace, and a parameter lineage graph. Every resolved field points to an exact source span and every unresolved field remains explicit. MethodChain does not turn missing evidence into a plausible recipe. The default path is deterministic, offline, and based on synthetic CC0 documents. It needs no API key, model endpoint, external database, or restricted publication. Current status MethodChain is a research prototype with a complete vertical slice. It is suitable for software evaluation, interface research, annotation studies, and extension with legally supplied document collections. It is not validated for laboratory execution and does not provide safety approval. documents.title: methodchain — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture MethodChain is organized around evidence-preserving transformations. Core data flow 1. A bundle loader validates access state and local paths 2. A parser converts readable files into typed document records 3. A citation detector classifies procedural inheritance claims 4. A search policy chooses the next legal document under a hard budget 5. An extractor creates direct protocol fields with exact spans 6. A work merger combines main text and inspected supplements 7. An aligner classifies parent-child parameter changes 8. A lineage builder connects final fields to all supporting evidence 9. Validators reject unsupported values and graph cycles 10. The inventory compiler checks declared local capability 11. Reporters write replayable JSON and a review-oriented human protocol Evidence is immutable The pipeline does not edit a source record after hashing it. Derived objects reference the source document hash and exact span. The final protocol is disposable. It can be regenerated from the bundle, configuration, and manifest. Inheritance policies Strict mode requires explicit unchanged language before an unreported child field can inherit a parent value. Permissive mode also accepts a high-confidence procedural citation. This mode keeps the claim span and remains distinguishable in the run manifest. Neither mode resolves a contradiction by selecting a value. Failure behavior Parsing warnings remain attached to the document. Inaccessible ancestors generate a request-user-document action. Missing fields remain missing. Duplicate incompatible values become contradictions.

documents.title: changepilot — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: ChangePilot ChangePilot is a version-aware migration workbench for Python projects. It finds API usage that crosses a dependency upgrade boundary, traces the affected local call graph, stages conservative edits, and rejects patches that change code outside the declared rewrite set. The repository contains two working surfaces: - An interactive web workbench for exploring the migration flow - A Python AST engine and command line interface for repository analysis ChangePilot is an early engineering prototype. It is useful for inspecting a focused upgrade and testing migration contracts. It is not a replacement for a project test suite or a general Python refactoring platform. What it does Given a source tree and a set of current and target dependency versions, ChangePilot performs four steps: 1. It selects API changes whose version boundary is crossed by the upgrade 2. It locates matching call sites with Python AST analysis 3. It follows reverse local calls to estimate the review surface 4. It applies only deterministic edits and verifies a closed patch contract Rules that need context-sensitive restructuring stay in the review queue. For example, a method rename can be safe enough for an automatic edit while a call shape rewrite remains manual. Try the workbench ``bash npm ci npm run dev ` Open the local URL printed by the development server. The sample workspace includes Pydantic and NumPy migration findings, a line-level patch preview, and contract verification. The browser workbench uses a lightweight source detector so it can run without a backend. The Python package is

documents.title: changepilot — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture ChangePilot separates evidence collection, mutation, and verification. This keeps the automatic patch surface small and makes failures easier to audit. Inputs The Python engine accepts: - A Python file or project path - Current dependency versions - Target dependency versions - A reviewed API change catalog The scanner does not infer installed versions from the active environment. Callers provide the version pair explicitly so an analysis run remains reproducible. Version path resolver Each ApiChange record defines one upgrade boundary. ``text library from version to version symbol replacement kind risk confidence auto fix documentation url match name ` A rule is selected when the current version is below to version and the requested target version reaches or crosses to version. This is a boundary model rather than a complete dependency solver. Pre-release ordering and nonstandard version schemes are outside the current scope. AST index ProjectIndex collects: - Import aliases - Classes derived from Pydantic BaseModel - Typed local names - Variables created by known pandas constructors - Function definitions - Direct calls between local functions FindingVisitor then evaluates only the rules selected for the requested version path. Receiver checks are conservative. An untyped object with a method named dict is not assumed to be a Pydantic model. Impact tracing The analyzer stores local call edges as caller - callee and reverses them for impact traversal. Each finding starts at its enclosing function. Breadth-first search follows reverse callers for at most three

documents.title: changepilot — docs/rule-authoring.md - part 1
documents.summary: Rule authoring API migration rules are executable claims. Treat each rule as production code rather than a search pattern. Acceptance checklist A new automatic rule must include: - The affected library - The first version where the change applies - The old and new symbol - An official upstream documentation URL - A risk level - A confidence value with a stated reason - A positive detection fixture - A negative fixture - An exact patch fixture - An idempotence test - A closed patch contract test A manual rule needs the same detection evidence but does not need an exact patch fixture. Automatic rule criteria Mark auto fix=True only when all of the following are true: - The replacement is local and deterministic - The edit does not require data flow inference - The edit does not alter argument evaluation order - The edit preserves manual finding lines - Reapplying the rule produces no change - The upstream migration notes support the replacement When any condition is unclear, route the finding to manual review. Confidence Confidence is a ranking signal, not permission to edit. Suggested interpretation: | Range | Meaning | |---|---| | 0.95 to 1.00 | Exact namespace or typed receiver match | | 0.80 to 0.94 | Strong structural evidence with a small ambiguity | | 0.60 to 0.79 | Heuristic receiver or call-shape evidence | | Below 0.60 | Do not add without improving the detector | Scores are currently expert estimates. Do not describe them as calibrated probabilities. Version boundaries Use the earliest target release where the old form is no longer supported or the migration

documents.title: memequiv — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: MemEquiv MemEquiv is an offline test harness for persistent agent memory. It asks a practical question: when two conversation histories are equivalent under a declared relation, does a memory system preserve the right facts, uncertainty, scope, provenance, and future behavior? The repository includes an immutable evidence ledger, a deterministic reference reducer, seven memory adapters, fifteen executable contracts, paired benchmark generation, counterexample minimization, statistical reporting, a typed API, a CLI, and an interactive Contract Explorer. The default path runs on CPU without provider credentials or model downloads. MemEquiv is a research prototype. Passing its contracts is evidence about the tested relations, not proof that a memory system is safe or correct in every deployment. Why this exists Ordinary recall accuracy can look healthy while a memory system quietly broadens a work preference, promotes an assistant statement into user evidence, drops an exception, or keeps an expired plan active. MemEquiv makes those failures executable. Each benchmark case contains a source history, a valid transformation, fixed future probes, and two expected relations: - A state relation over canonical memory assertions - A behavior relation over deterministic probe responses Raw adapter state and source evidence stay attached to every comparison. Canonicalization supports cross-adapter analysis without replacing the audit trail. documents.summary: API, and web catalog: `bash memequiv list-contracts memequiv list-adapters ` Evidence ledger Ledger events are immutable and hash chained. A database trigger rejects update and delete operations. Corrections append new evidence and preserve the superseded event. The reducer materializes a current profile while retaining: - Speaker authority and source type - Scope and scope hierarchy - Modality, polarity, negation, and confidence - Temporal validity - Exceptions and contradictions - Correction and supersession edges - Derivation links to source events Snapshots contain integrity metadata and reject incompatible or corrupted restores. Inspect, minimize, and replay After a run, inspect a recorded finding: `bash memequiv inspect <run-id <violation-id \ --store artifacts/runs/smoke-results.duckdb ` Minimize it: `bash memequiv minimize <run-id <violation-id \ --store artifacts/runs/smoke-results.duckdb \ --output artifacts/runs/reproducer.json ` Replay the portable bundle: `bash memequiv replay artifacts/runs/reproducer.json ` The minimizer removes sessions, turns, clauses, filler, probes, and transformation operations only when contract applicability and the observed violation remain intact. Each accepted or rejected step is recorded in the replay bundle. Reports and claims Generate a report from an existing run: `bash memequiv report <run-id \ --store artifacts/runs/smoke-results.duckdb \ --output artifacts/runs/<run-id /report.md ` Reporting includes: - Macro and micro violation rates - Severity-weighted analysis - Ordinary personalization accuracy - Base-history cluster

documents.title: currigraph — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: <div align="center" CurriGraph Learn the transfer graph. Select the next experience. Explain every decision. ![Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/) ![Tests]( validation) ![License](LICENSE) </div CurriGraph is an end-to-end research prototype for online curriculum selection in tool agents. It estimates how practice on one task family changes performance on another, represents those estimates as a directed transfer graph, and uses the graph to choose the next experience under a fixed execution budget. The central hypothesis is simple: A curriculum should optimize expected downstream learning, not only immediate uncertainty, difficulty, or diversity. CurriGraph makes this hypothesis testable. It ships with a deterministic synthetic environment, a fixed memory learner, matched transfer probes, eight non-oracle schedulers, an oracle upper bound, replayable logs, a local studio, and a public interactive demo. This repository is a research prototype. Synthetic results are diagnostics, not evidence of general performance on real agents. What works - Directed transfer estimates with uncertainty and negative-transfer risk - Online task selection with an auditable score decomposition - Deterministic task execution and verifier-gated outcomes - A fixed retrieve, solve, consolidate memory learner across every scheduler - Matched transfer probes with logged selection propensities - Verifier-gated task variant generation - Random, difficulty, uncertainty, diversity, learning-progress, hybrid, and oracle baselines - SQLite and JSONL run storage - Replayable evaluation from immutable

documents.title: currigraph — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture CurriGraph separates environment truth, learned state, and policy state so curriculum comparisons remain interpretable. Component boundaries Task registry The registry owns immutable task specifications and split labels. It rejects duplicate task identifiers and returns candidates in stable order. Environment TransferGym owns the hidden directed transfer graph and deterministic execution model. The scheduler never receives hidden edges unless the oracle policy is selected. Fixed memory learner Every scheduler uses the same retrieve, solve, consolidate implementation. Successful verified tasks update skill competence. Failed tasks can add failure insights but cannot promote a skill procedure. Transfer graph The learned graph stores one posterior per ordered family pair: - posterior mean - posterior standard deviation - positive and negative evidence counts - negative-transfer risk - evidence identifiers Matched probes update edges with a Gaussian conjugate approximation. Repeated evidence lowers uncertainty. Scheduler Schedulers receive only the task registry, learned graph, memory state, remaining budget, and logged history. The CurriGraph policy combines downstream value, information gain, coverage, uncertainty, cost, and negative risk. Verifier The verifier is the only authority for task success. Task generation cannot add a candidate until its verifier contract is valid and the synthetic oracle confirms solvability. Storage SQLite supports local inspection. JSONL files are the portable replay format. Metrics are derived products and can be regenerated from

documents.title: communicate-to-remember — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: Communicate to Remember Joint communication and memory routing for multi-agent systems. ![CI](https://github.com/pxnkit/communicate-to-remember/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![License: MIT](LICENSE) ![Node 22](package.json) ![Live demo](https://communicate-to-remember.brahmkhatripankit.chatgpt.site) Communicate to Remember is an executable research prototype for a narrow question: Given one claim, observation, or procedure, should the system drop it, send it to one agent, broadcast it, keep it local, or store it for the team? The router also selects recipients and a time to live. It learns from later outcomes while the agents that produced the information remain frozen. The repository includes a live lifecycle dashboard, a server-side simulation API, a contextual-bandit controller, seven budget-matched baselines, deterministic evaluation, and automated tests. Why this project exists Communication and memory are often configured as separate subsystems. That separation creates predictable waste: - Information is broadcast even when one recipient needs it - Private context enters shared memory - Low-quality claims persist longer than their evidence supports - Useful procedures expire before recurring tasks need them - Store-all policies accumulate noise and increase retrieval latency This project treats communication and persistence as one per-item routing decision. System model For every information item, the controller observes: - Immediate usefulness - Expected future reuse - Team relevance - Privacy risk - Negative-transfer risk - Provenance quality - Cost sensitivity It

documents.title: communicate-to-remember — docs/methodology.md - part 1
documents.summary: Methodology Objective The router maximizes useful information delivery and reuse under a shared communication and storage budget. Each item has one observed feature vector: ``text x = [ immediate usefulness, future reuse, team relevance, 1 - privacy risk, 1 - negative-transfer risk, provenance, 1 - cost sensitivity ] ` The action space contains drop, unicast, broadcast, local memory, and shared memory. Controller The controller keeps an independent ridge-regression model for each action. At decision time it computes an upper-confidence score: `text score(a) = theta a^T x + alpha sqrt(x^T A a^-1 x) - risk(a) - cost(a) ` Selective forced exploration replaces the greedy action with a uniformly sampled action at the configured probability. After the lifecycle outcome is known, the selected action model receives the scalar reward. TTL selection Communication routes receive a one-episode delivery TTL. Memory routes select from: `text 1 | 3 | 8 | 20 episodes `` The TTL score balances expected reuse coverage, remaining budget, privacy risk, and negative-transfer risk. Reward Positive components: - Immediate usefulness delivered to an appropriate scope - Future reuse observed before expiry - Correct disposal of a low-value item Negative components: - Communication and storage cost - Privacy exposure from a broad route - Negative transfer from broad irrelevant context - Failure to serve an eligible immediate or future use Budget matching Every policy receives one budget. When the next proposed action would exceed the remaining budget, that action becomes drop. This rule is applied to

documents.title: scopeguard — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: <div align="center" ScopeGuard Memory non-interference for tool-using agents ScopeGuard attributes memory influence at the tool-argument level, checks that influence against explicit scope and authority, repairs unauthorized changes, and writes a signed audit trace. Live demo · Method · Proxy API · Reproducibility ![Python](pyproject.toml) ![Tests](tests) ![License](LICENSE) ![No API key](configs/demo small.yaml) </div The contract A memory may change a tool argument only when its declared scope, source, authority, purpose, and evidence permit that exact influence. Memory retrieval answers what might be useful. ScopeGuard answers what is authorized to affect execution. For a protected argument a and an out-of-scope memory m, the deterministic contract is: ``text d(f(q, T, M)[a], f(q, T, M \ {m})[a]) <= epsilon a ` When the observed distance exceeds the policy threshold, ScopeGuard creates a memory-to-argument influence edge and enforces the declared response. Why argument-level enforcement A whole memory can contain both useful and unauthorized signals. A timezone preference may be valid for timezone while a personal cost preference must not reduce priority in the same project call. ScopeGuard keeps these decisions separate: | Memory influence | Argument policy | Outcome | |---|---|---| | Explicit timezone preference changes timezone | Personalizable and correctly scoped | Permit | | Personal risk preference changes visibility | Protected and out of scope | Repair | | Inferred language preference changes language | Relevant but below required authority | Clarify | |

documents.title: scopeguard — docs/METHOD.md - part 1
documents.summary: ScopeGuard method Problem definition Let an agent generate a fixed-schema tool call from a user request, tool schema, and retrieved memory set. ``text C = f(q, T, M) ` The call C contains arguments a 1 through a k. A memory may be useful for one argument and unauthorized for another. ScopeGuard therefore evaluates influence at the memory-to-argument edge, not at the whole-memory level. Each memory is a MemoryCard with: - declared scope domains - applicable tools and arguments - source and authority - intended purpose - expiration conditions - supporting evidence - a content hash Each tool is governed by a ToolPolicy with: - protected and personalizable arguments - safe defaults - allowed memory sources and scopes - minimum authority - an argument-specific violation action Counterfactual attribution ScopeGuard generates the original call with all retrieved memories. It then removes one memory at a time and regenerates the call under the same seed. For memory m i and argument a j: `text I(m i, a j) = d(C[a j], C without m i[a j]) ` The distance function is type-aware: - booleans and categories use exact change - numbers use normalized distance - lists use Jaccard distance - strings use normalized edit distance - objects use recursive field distance An InfluenceEdge is created when the distance exceeds the argument threshold. Scope and authority Every edge is checked by a deterministic policy function: `text check scope(memory, tool policy, argument, request context) ` The result is one of: - allowed - denied - expired - insufficient authority - ambiguous Relevance alone never

documents.summary: grants authority. A memory can be relevant to the broad task and still lack permission to change a particular argument. Enforcement The enforcement engine chooses the action declared for the affected argument: - permit - repair to the no-memory value - repair to a safe default - strip the memory and regenerate the argument - ask a clarification question - block execution The engine repairs only affected arguments. Authorized values on unrelated arguments remain intact. Signed traces Every intercepted call produces an InfluenceTrace` containing: - original and final calls - counterfactual calls - argument differences - influence edges - scope verdicts - decision details - memory content hashes - policy version - latency The trace is serialized with sorted JSON keys and compact separators. The signature field is excluded from canonicalization. HMAC-SHA256 signs the remaining payload. Raw memory text is not stored in a trace by default.

documents.summary: Memory non-interference Deterministic property Let a be a protected argument and let m be a memory that is out of scope for a. For a deterministic agent with fixed request, tool schema, policy, and seed: ``text d(f(q, T, M)[a], f(q, T, M \ {m})[a]) <= epsilon a ` The default offline simulator uses epsilon a = 0 for booleans and categorical values. Numeric and structured arguments may use a policy-specific tolerance. If the observed distance exceeds the threshold, ScopeGuard creates an influence edge and enforces the argument policy. Stochastic property For stochastic agents, compare argument distributions over repeated samples: `text D(P(a | q, T, M), P(a | q, T, M \ {m})) <= epsilon a `` The adapter boundary supports repeated samples. The default project does not require a stochastic model. Protected arguments Protected arguments commonly control: - visibility and privacy - deletion and mutation method - approval and review gates - validation depth - rollback and recovery - logging and audit coverage - safety filtering - authentication and trust checks - financial or compute commitments Protection is declared by the tool policy. Argument names alone are not treated as a complete risk model. Selective checking Selective mode evaluates protected and personalizable arguments first. Exhaustive mode compares every argument. The ablation configuration exposes both modes.
