documents.title: worldmodel-lstar — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: WorldModel-L ![Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/) ![License: MIT](LICENSE) ![Offline first]( quickstart) WorldModel-L is a research prototype for learning hidden tool behavior before an agent commits to a plan. The system combines bounded semantic proposals with an explicit symbolic version space. It selects experiments by expected hypothesis elimination or information gain, turns prediction failures into constraints, and blocks model-dependent plans while relevant uncertainty remains. The default build is local, deterministic, and complete. It does not need an API key, a GPU, a model download, or a live service. Why this project exists Tool agents often act before they understand the environment they are changing. A failed call may reveal a hidden precondition, an expiring token, an order constraint, or an irreversible side effect. Prompt history alone does not provide a reliable representation of those rules. WorldModel-L makes uncertainty concrete. - Every candidate world model is inspectable - Every experiment has an information score, cost, risk, and reversibility flag - Every observation removes inconsistent candidates - Every counterexample becomes a local symbolic constraint - Every planning decision records why execution was allowed or blocked - Every run writes a reproducible evidence bundle System overview ``mermaid flowchart LR A["Bounded semantic proposals"] -- B["Symbolic candidate compiler"] B -- C["Weighted version space"] C -- D["Risk-aware experiment selector"] D -- E["Hidden tool environment"] E -- F["Observation and counterexample"] F -- C C --

documents.title: worldmodel-lstar — docs/METHOD.md - part 1
documents.summary: Method Problem definition Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be a bounded family of deterministic world models and let \(M^\star\) be the hidden environment. An experiment \(e\) is an action sequence with observable outcome \(o\), cost \(c(e)\), risk \(r(e)\), and a reversibility indicator. The learner maintains a posterior over a version space \[ V t = \{M \in \mathcal{M} \mid M \text{ is consistent with } D t\} \] where \(D t\) is the set of experiments and observations collected through step \(t\). The implementation supports exact DFA candidates and bounded guarded-transition parameter grids. Small spaces are enumerated. Larger spaces can be represented by a beam of repaired candidates. Candidate compilation A candidate is a typed symbolic record with states, transitions, guards, invariants, posterior mass, and provenance. DFA candidates compile to a total transition function. Hidden REST candidates compile to a deterministic simulator with explicit latent parameters. Free-form model output is never executed. Optional language-model output is parsed against a small JSON schema, converted into candidate edits, and checked against every observation. Active experiments For each available experiment, the version space predicts a partition of candidates by outcome. If \(V o\) is the group that predicts outcome \(o\), expected elimination is \[ \sum o p(o) \left(|V| - |V o|\right) \] The information-gain alternative is \[ H(V) - \sum o p(o)H(V \mid o) \] The production score subtracts cost, risk, and irreversibility penalties. This lets a safe dry run outrank an irreversible operation even

documents.title: worldmodel-lstar — docs/METHOD.md - part 2
documents.summary: when both are informative. Counterexample repair An equivalence failure or unexpected tool response produces a counterexample record. The repair path performs four operations. 1. Find the first mismatching response in the predicted and observed traces 2. Convert the mismatch into a prefix constraint 3. Remove candidates that violate the constraint 4. Propose local state, transition, guard, or abstraction edits Only repaired candidates that satisfy the complete evidence set may re-enter the version space. Planning gate The gate evaluates uncertainty in relation to one proposed plan. Global exact recovery is sufficient but not always necessary. Planning is allowed when remaining models agree on the plan outcome, confidence thresholds are satisfied, or the immediate action is safe and reversible. This distinction matters in large model spaces. An agent may not need to identify every hidden rule when all plausible models support the same low-risk action. Environment change The drift detector maintains a bounded prediction-error window. A sustained error rate reopens a local candidate neighborhood around the current model. Unaffected parameters are preserved. Change evaluation compares local edit queries with full relearning queries and reports retained model structure. Complexity Exact DFA enumeration grows exponentially with state count and is intended for controlled small systems. The practical path for larger systems is a candidate beam with typed local edits, semantic priors, and targeted experiment generation. The repository makes this limitation visible. It does not

documents.title: worldmodel-lstar — docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md - part 1
documents.summary: Environments Execution model Every experiment is an action sequence executed from a clean deterministic state. The reset boundary provides comparable evidence and prevents one probe from contaminating another. An observation records the experiment, action sequence, normalized result, cost, visible state, errors, side effects, and a logical timestamp. Binary DFA The DFA oracle supports membership queries and equivalence queries. Equivalence failures return the shortest distinguishing word found by breadth-first search over the product automaton. Fixtures cover suffix, parity, and substring languages. A seeded random generator is also available. Token expiry Hidden parameters control the number of protected calls allowed by a token and whether refresh resets token age. The agent can test protected endpoints before login, near expiry, after expiry, and around refresh. Order workflow The environment models cart creation, item insertion, checkout, confirmation, and cancellation. Confirmation creates an irreversible side effect. Risk-aware selection penalizes direct confirmation probes. Hidden quota Cheap and deep searches consume different hidden quota amounts. Repeated and mixed sequences reveal capacity and weighted cost. Retry policy The first unstable call fails. A successful retry requires hidden backoff. Premature retries may extend the cooldown. Stateful permissions Viewer, editor, and admin roles interact with resource state. Edit and publish permissions are separate. Publication creates a side effect. documents.summary: LineageRAG Copy-aware evidence corroboration for retrieval-augmented verification ![Python 3.11+](https://www.python.org/) ![License: MIT](LICENSE) ![Offline first]( quick-start) LineageRAG asks a simple question before treating agreement as confidence: Did these documents reach the same conclusion independently, or did they copy one another? Twenty pages can repeat one mistaken bulletin. A verifier that counts URLs sees twenty witnesses. LineageRAG infers likely derivation links, collapses dependent documents into origin families, and combines evidence at the family level. The repository is a complete CPU-only research system. It generates controlled evidence cascades, trains a calibrated dependency classifier, infers sparse document genealogy, trains dataset-specific stance models, runs copy-aware Bayesian verification, compares baselines, and produces an interactive evidence graph. Smoke mode needs no API key, GPU, model download, or external dataset. Why source count is not evidence count Domain and URL deduplication address repeated locations. Near-duplicate filtering catches almost identical text. Neither is enough when copied information crosses domains, receives a heavy rewrite, preserves a rare factual error, or cites a common upstream report. LineageRAG estimates dependence from observable signals: - publication order - citation and quotation links - exact and paraphrased text overlap - stable SimHash similarity - entity and number overlap - shared rare error markers - URL, domain, and title similarity The resulting weighted graph is clustered into likely origin

documents.summary: remains available for offline smoke tests. Edges above the calibrated threshold form a directed graph. Explicit citations determine direction first, followed by publication order. Copy-family inference keeps at most one parent per document to reduce bridge errors. Within each predicted family $f$, document stances are pooled into a family score $s f \in [-1, 1]$. The support posterior is: `math \mathrm{logit}\,P(y=1 \mid E) = \mathrm{logit}\,P(y=1) + \sum f 1.6\,w f\,s f ` The effective family weight grows slowly with copied descendants: `math w f = c f \min \left( 1 + \alpha \log(1 + |f| - 1), \tau \right) ` Here $c f$ combines stance confidence, lineage confidence, and configurable source reliability. The cap $\tau$ is the key safeguard. One family cannot gain unbounded influence by producing more copies. Dataset-specific stance classifiers use TF-IDF features and logistic regression. Training, validation, and test claims are disjoint. Each method receives its own validation-fitted claim-probability calibrator. Inference receives documents and extracted stances only. Oracle files are read during metric calculation and by explicit upper-bound baselines. documents.title: lineagerag — docs/dataset_card.md
documents.summary: Synthetic evidence cascade dataset card Purpose The bundled generator tests whether a verifier distinguishes repeated documents from independent evidence. It is designed for software validation, controlled ablations, and failure analysis. Composition The default smoke configuration generates 200 claims and more than 2,000 documents across nine graph templates. Each claim has observed documents and stance observations. Oracle edges, families, and stances are written to separate files. Generation All people, organizations, projects, domains, and events are fictional. Text is assembled from repository-authored templates and deterministic mutations. Intended use - lineage inference unit tests - copy-robust verification research - calibration experiments - active retrieval policy tests Out-of-scope use The dataset must not be used to claim real-world fact-checking performance, source credibility, political truthfulness, or misinformation prevalence. Known bias Synthetic rare-error markers and regular publication times make some derivation links easier than natural data. The language is narrow and does not represent multilingual, scientific, social, or adversarial writing. External evaluation data The real-data protocol for SciFact, AVeriTeC, and OpenAlex is documented in real data.md. None of those raw sources are distributed with this repository.

documents.title: lineagerag — docs/model_card.md
documents.summary: LineageRAG model card Model details LineageRAG 0.1 is a deterministic pipeline rather than a trained foundation model. It uses hand-specified pair features, a logistic edge score, graph connected components, lexical stance observations, and a bounded family-level Bayesian verifier. Inputs - a claim - retrieved documents - publication metadata - citations and quotations when available - stance observations Outputs - predicted claim label - support probability - raw support and refute counts - effective family-level counts - predicted lineage edges and families - false-corroboration risk - independent-search intent Performance No fixed performance values are shipped as scientific claims. Run the benchmark to produce versioned local metrics. Synthetic smoke results are engineering checks only. Limitations The edge model is not calibrated for open-web data. The lexical stance extractor cannot handle nuanced entailment. Connected-component clustering is sensitive to bridge errors. Publication times can be missing or manipulated. Source reliability defaults are illustrative. Ethical considerations The system should support human review, not automate credibility judgments about people or publishers. Family inference is probabilistic and can incorrectly associate independent authors. Preserve source context and provide an appeal path in any applied system.

documents.title: lineagerag — docs/real_data.md - part 1
documents.summary: Real data protocol LineageRAG uses three external research resources. Their raw files and cached API responses are excluded from Git. The repository stores only acquisition metadata, normalization code, and derived aggregate results. SciFact SciFact provides scientific claims, document abstracts, document-level stance labels, and sentence rationales. The official development set is the untouched test set. The final 20 percent of training claim IDs form the validation set. The claim and annotation files use CC BY 4.0. Corpus abstracts use ODC-By 1.0. See the official SciFact repository. SciFact does not provide a trustworthy claim publication date. Its experiment is therefore an official split, not a temporal split. AVeriTeC AVeriTeC provides real web claims, claim dates, verdicts, and annotated question and answer evidence with source URLs. Claims from the official train and development files are sorted by parsed claim date and divided chronologically into 70 percent training, 15 percent validation, and 15 percent test. Document stance is weak supervision. Each annotated evidence document inherits the claim-level verdict for model training and scoring. This is noisier than SciFact's direct document stance labels and is reported as a limitation. AVeriTeC uses CC BY-NC 4.0. The project is research-only with respect to this data. See the official AVeriTeC repository. OpenAlex SciFact evidence-paper titles are matched to OpenAlex works. documents.title: robustask — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: RobustAsk RobustAsk is an offline research framework for clarification when a user answer may be wrong. Most clarification systems model a missing value and assume that asking reveals useful information. RobustAsk treats the answer as an observation from an uncertain channel. The controller estimates field values, user reliability, systematic confusion, and fatigue before it chooses whether to ask, rephrase, cross-check, use a deterministic verifier, act, or abstain. The repository is designed for reproducible systems research. The default benchmark needs no API key, GPU, model download, or external dataset. Research status This is a runnable research prototype with a paper scaffold. It is not presented as a completed paper result. The built-in smoke run checks installation, policy behavior, metrics, plots, and artifact contracts. Its sample is intentionally small. A successful smoke criterion is evidence that the experiment is worth scaling, not evidence that the research claim is established. The first frozen five-seed BookSafe study is reported in results/booksafe 5seed/README.md. It substantially reduced catastrophic errors in the configured synthetic test, but missed the truthful-user non-inferiority margin. The recorded kill criterion is therefore not met. What is implemented - Exact discrete inference over task fields and terminal goals - Beta reliability posteriors for each user-provided field - Dirichlet-style categorical confusion counts - A fatigue adjustment in reliability logit space - Hard reliability updates after deterministic verification - Fractional

A normal controller receives only: - the public task schema - priors and constraints - observations emitted by an allowed interaction - its current belief state - the remaining interaction budget It does not receive the simulator profile label, true field values, or oracle decision. Oracle policies are isolated by name and receive evaluator-only context that normal policies never see. Decision rule For belief state $b$, the risk of stopping is ``math R(b) = \min d \mathbb{E} {h \sim b}[L(d, h)] ` For an information action $a$, RobustAsk scores a conservative decision-risk reduction `math \mathrm{RVSI}(a) = \min {\rho \in \mathcal{C}(b)} \mathbb{E} {o \mid a, \rho} \left[R(b) - R(b^{a,o})\right] - c {\mathrm{burden}}(a) - c {\mathrm{tool}}(a) ` $\mathcal{C}(b)$ is a small grid drawn from the current Beta credible interval. documents.summary: RobustAsk synthetic benchmark card Summary RobustAsk includes two generated benchmark families for testing clarification under answer-channel uncertainty. ToyLogic contains small boolean constraint tasks with one to three unavailable values. BookSafe contains synthetic parameterized actions for booking, refund, account update, medical intake, and form submission scenarios. Critical parameter errors receive a larger loss. Data generation Tasks are generated locally from explicit domains and seeded NumPy random generators. Every task has: - a controller-visible TaskSpec - an evaluator-only HiddenState - a public mapping from complete assignments to terminal decisions - an explicit loss matrix No external dataset is required or downloaded. User channels Profiles are parameterized observation channels. They control accuracy, uncertainty, contradiction, confidence, fatigue, and categorical confusion. Held-out mixtures combine mechanisms that are not used for threshold tuning. Intended use - controller development - regression tests for belief updates - safety-oriented policy comparisons - calibration and selective-risk experiments Out-of-scope use - medical decision support - financial transactions - real account updates - claims about human behavior without validation - ranking or judging individual users Known limitations The language is templated. Field domains are small. Profiles are synthetic. The benchmark does not capture social context, strategic deception, accessibility needs, cultural variation, or natural conversational repair. documents.title: robustask — docs/model_card.md
documents.summary: RobustAsk controller card Model details RobustAsk is a deterministic Bayesian decision controller. It is not a pretrained language model. It maintains: - categorical posteriors over fields - a posterior over terminal goals - Beta reliability parameters per field - categorical confusion counts - a simple fatigue state - a full observation log Inputs - public task schema - constraints and priors - allowed observations - interaction budget Outputs One typed action: - ask - rephrase - cross-check - tool - act - abstain Objective The controller minimizes posterior expected terminal loss. Information actions are selected by conservative expected risk reduction over a small reliability credible set, less burden and tool cost. Safety properties - simulator truth is outside the controller schema - deterministic verification is explicitly costed - abstention is available when residual risk is high - every random component is seeded - trajectories expose the controller's belief before and after observations Limitations Exact enumeration scales poorly with many fields. Reliability priors affect behavior. Fractional reliability learning is not identifiable without additional assumptions. The fatigue model is not fitted to human data. The controller does not parse free-form language.

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture FALSIFY is an offline-first research system for finding where a learned tool-use procedure becomes harmful. Execution boundary The trusted runtime contains the contract compiler, registered mutation operators, deterministic fixture tools, outcome checks, and artifact writers. Model text, trajectories, procedure records, task contracts, and imported manifests are untrusted inputs. The sandbox accepts structured actions only. A call names a registered tool and supplies arguments that must pass its current schema. No input can inject source code into the runtime. Main data flow 1. A successful observable trajectory is converted into a typed procedure 2. The source task is compiled into tools, state, constraints, and exact checks 3. A search policy selects typed mutation programs 4. The compiler rejects invalid or unsatisfiable descendants 5. Legal descendants run through matched control and treatment branches 6. Exact replay validates that the intervention label is stable 7. Harmful cases enter the minimizer 8. Safe and harmful examples train a procedure-specific risk model 9. A held-out calibration group defines the selective threshold 10. The controller requires contract compatibility and acceptable risk State and replay Each branch starts from an independent deep copy of the compiled initial state. Every tool call produces: - Action and validated arguments - Observation code and bounded payload - State hash before the call - State hash after the call - Top-level state diff - Recorded side effects - Hard constraint violations No-op replay executes the same

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/estimands.md - part 1
documents.summary: Estimands and labels Direct procedure effect For task contract x, procedure p, and matched seed u, define: ``text effect(p, x, u) = utility(treatment) - utility(control) `` The control branch uses the contract-aware general agent. The treatment branch executes the frozen procedure. Both branches use the same compiled task, initial state, environment version, seed, and resource limits. Utility combines exact task success, hard violations, execution cost, and a fixed planning overhead. The overhead is versioned and identical across runs in one experiment. Negative transfer A procedure causes negative transfer when the control branch reaches the goal and treatment either: - Lowers utility beyond the registered margin - Violates a hard contract - Becomes unexecutable because a required tool or schema changed Both-branches-fail and environment-failure cases are not procedure counterexamples. Minimum counterexample A certified counterexample must be legal, solvable, replay-valid, and harmful. Minimization removes registered operators while preserving those conditions. The implementation claims local minimality under the registered mutation grammar. It does not claim global minimality over natural-language tasks. Selective deployment Coverage is the fraction of evaluated descendants on which the gate uses the procedure. Selective risk is the negative-transfer rate among those accepted descendants. The finite-sample risk bound applies only to the registered exchangeable operator mixture. Operator holdout and environment shift are empirical OOD evaluations without the same

documents.title: regimebank — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: RegimeBank RegimeBank gives a lifelong agent separate memories for operating regimes that can disappear and later return. Most memory policies assume that recent experience is always the most relevant. That assumption breaks on streams such as API v1, API v2, then API v1 again. A sliding window must relearn the first API. A global memory can mix incompatible procedures. RegimeBank detects the change, keeps the memories separate, and reactivates the earlier bank when the first regime returns. The repository is runnable on a laptop. It includes a recurring contextual-bandit benchmark, Bayesian online change-point detection, regime-aware memory, six baselines, an oracle, metrics, plots, tests, and a JSONL adapter for real agent traces. !Benchmark output What is implemented - Bayesian online change-point detection with a multivariate Student-t predictive model - Episodic memory for concrete task, action, and outcome records - Procedural memory with one regularized reward model per action - An invariant pool for action evidence validated in more than one regime - Regime reactivation from learned signal prototypes - Posterior-weighted retrieval when regime identity is uncertain - Bank merging only after validation succeeds in both directions - Abrupt, gradual, cyclic, and recurring schedules - API, tool-schema, and hidden-transition synthetic domains - Global, sliding-window, reservoir, periodic-deletion, exponential-decay, and oracle baselines - Prequential and recurrence-focused evaluation - Reproducible CSV, JSON, and PNG artifacts Quick start RegimeBank requires Python 3.11

documents.title: regimebank — docs/design.md - part 1
documents.summary: RegimeBank design Goal RegimeBank handles streams where an operating regime can disappear and later return. It separates change detection from regime recognition: - Change detection asks whether the current generating process changed - Regime recognition asks whether the new process matches a bank seen before That distinction is the core design decision. Signal model At step \(t\), the detector receives: \[ x t = [s t, e t, d t, o {t-1}, \epsilon {t-1}, a {t-1}] \] where: - \(s t\) is the tool-schema fingerprint - \(e t\) is the task embedding - \(d t\) is the current transition-error signature - \(o {t-1}\) is the previous outcome - \(\epsilon {t-1}\) is the previous prediction error - \(a {t-1}\) is memory agreement The reference environment scales stable schema features more strongly than task context. This makes visible API changes easy to identify while preserving outcome-based evidence for hidden transition changes. Bayesian online change-point detection The detector maintains a posterior over run length: \[ p(r t \mid x {1:t}) \] Every run length has an independent Normal-Inverse-Gamma model per signal dimension. Integrating the unknown mean and variance gives a Student-t predictive density. A constant hazard controls the prior probability of a boundary. The implementation truncates run length to a configurable maximum. This bounds memory and update cost without changing the public interface. Regime recognition Every bank stores an online signal prototype. After a detected change, RegimeBank compares the new signal with all inactive prototypes. The posterior combines

documents.title: regimebank — docs/design.md - part 2
documents.summary: prototype distance and a small usage prior. If no inactive bank clears the reactivation threshold, the manager creates a new bank. The current bank does not compete in the reactivation decision. A detected change cannot be silently absorbed back into the same bank. Episodic memory An episode stores: - Context - Action - Observed reward - Detector signal - Stream step - Utility - Retrieval count Retrieval uses squared Euclidean distance in normalized context space. A bounded bank retains higher-utility and repeatedly useful episodes. Procedural memory Each bank maintains a regularized linear reward model for every action: \[ \hat{\theta} a = A a^{-1} b a \] with: \[ A a = \lambda I + \sum i x i x i^T \] \[ b a = \sum i r i x i \] Procedural and episodic predictions are blended. The procedural weight increases as a bank gains experience. Invariant memory The invariant pool tracks action evidence by bank. An action prior becomes invariant only after it has enough observations in at least two regimes and each validated regime has non-trivial success. The invariant contribution is deliberately small. It supports transfer without overriding regime-specific procedures. Posterior-weighted retrieval When the regime posterior is diffuse, RegimeBank queries every candidate bank and combines action scores using posterior mass. This avoids a brittle early switch. Once one bank dominates, the same equation naturally behaves like hard routing. Merge guard Two inactive banks can merge only when all conditions hold: 1. Their signal prototypes are sufficiently similar 2. The left bank

Complexity Let \(R\) be the run-length cap, \(d\) the signal dimension, \(B\) the number of banks, and \(K\) the retrieval count. - Detector update is \(O(Rd)\) - Regime scoring is \(O(Bd)\) - Procedural prediction is \(O(Ad c^3)\) with small context dimension \(d c\) - Episodic retrieval is linear in bank capacity in this reference implementation Approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval can replace the linear scan without changing the manager.

documents.title: memintervene — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: MemIntervene Replay-defined credit assignment for memory lifecycle operations in long-horizon agents. MemIntervene is an offline-first research and engineering system for answering a narrow question: which memory record, representation, link, or lifecycle operation changed a later agent decision? It treats credit as a paired intervention over a versioned memory state—not as retrieval frequency, attention, citation, or terminal reward alone. The repository is a complete deterministic vertical slice: immutable event ledger, rebuildable memory views, typed interventions, four replay modes, exact effects, controlled-direct and total-system estimands, Shapley and interaction diagnostics, a calibrated effect predictor, a conservative fixed-budget policy, FastAPI, React/TypeScript replay console, tests, Docker, CI, and generated paper assets. Python dependencies are resolved in requirements.lock; web dependencies and approved build scripts are frozen in apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml. Research status: the software path is complete and verified; the current MiniMemIntervene run is a smoke-scale result, not a publication claim. The learned policy ties the strongest fixed baseline on the held-out synthetic split, so the policy kill criterion is not met. Why this project exists Long-horizon memory systems can fail in ways that retrieval-only evaluation misses: - a retrieved record may be redundant and have no marginal effect; - an unretrieved record can displace the decisive record from top-k; - a summary can drop a number or remove harmful noise; - a stale preference

Memory views are deterministic functions of ledger history. 4. Derived records preserve source and parent lineage. 5. Forgetting and quarantine affect the active view but remain reversible in the research ledger. 6. Controlled-direct and total-system effects are never combined without labels. 7. Invalid or off-manifold replay is typed and excluded rather than silently scored. 8. The default action path never reads the benchmark's correct answer; only the environment scores it. documents.title: certicompress — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: CertiCompress CertiCompress is a working research and engineering system for proof-carrying memory consolidation in action-coupled agents. Long-running agents collect more history than they can serve efficiently. A short summary can save tokens, but a fluent summary is not enough when memory changes tool calls, safety decisions, schedules, budgets, or user preferences. CertiCompress treats every consolidation as an untrusted proposal. A proposal becomes active only after it passes typed semantic checks, provenance checks, and deterministic behavior replay. The project runs fully offline. It includes an append-only event ledger, deletable encrypted payloads, lineage tracking, nine consolidation operators, three replay levels, certificate lifecycle management, rate-distortion optimization, a FastAPI service, a React research console, tests, Docker support, generated reports, and a reproducible technical paper. What the system guarantees For the included deterministic fixtures, an active derived memory has: - Exact source event and source span references - Typed checks for negation, modality, dates, numbers, units, preferences, and control-text injection - Controlled direct, bounded horizon, and total system replay evidence - A versioned certificate bound to the candidate, probes, dependencies, and verifier outputs - Automatic raw-memory fallback when evidence is missing or a dependency becomes stale A certificate is evidence for a finite test distribution and a specific dependency manifest. It is not a universal proof that two language model systems behave identically in

documents.title: certicompress — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture CertiCompress separates the write path, evidence path, and serving path. Write path The SQLite ledger accepts typed events through an append-only API. Each record binds parent events, logical time, schema version, model dependencies, and a content hash. Raw text is written to an encrypted payload store and referenced by ID. Deleting a payload does not rewrite the ledger. The optional SQLAlchemy projection and Alembic migration provide a conventional integration point for larger services. Evidence path Deterministic extraction emits exact source spans and typed claims. The lineage graph records every derivation. Candidate generation applies all nine operators through one typed contract. Verification has four layers: 1. Typed preservation checks 2. Deterministic semantic stance checks 3. Exact provenance and ancestry checks 4. Paired behavior replay The certificate authority combines these results with dependency versions and risk bounds. The integrity hash covers the complete certificate body. Serving path Only a candidate with a valid certificate can become active. The per-case selector prefers the smallest eligible candidate. The global optimizer chooses at most one candidate per case under an active-rate budget and distortion bound. Invalidation is dependency-aware. A source event or version change marks only affected certificates stale. The serving path falls back to raw memory until a fresh certificate becomes active. Storage choices SQLite keeps the reference implementation easy to run and audit. The store interfaces are narrow enough to replace with

documents.title: tempo-trust — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: TEMPO-Trust Claim-conditioned online source reliability for evidence systems that operate under drift, copying, and delayed feedback. TEMPO-Trust answers a practical question: what should an evidence agent do when a source that has been reliable in general becomes unreliable for one topic? The system keeps trust local to source, topic, claim type, time, and detected regime. It converts documents into atomic claims, scores evidence stance, groups dependent sources before aggregation, detects abrupt reliability changes, and abstains when independent support is too weak. Every state transition and answer decision is recorded in a checksummed provenance ledger. This repository includes the research core, a deterministic streaming benchmark, a FastAPI service, a React dashboard, evaluation and calibration utilities, dataset adapters, paper asset generation, tests, containers, and CI. Why this project exists A single reputation score is too coarse for a changing evidence environment. A source may remain accurate on climate policy while failing on medicine. Several sites may repeat the same upstream report and appear to provide independent confirmation. Audits may arrive late or never arrive. A safe system must update online without using future labels, distinguish copying from corroboration, detect meaningful changes, and expose the evidence behind every decision. TEMPO-Trust is designed around those requirements. System behavior ``mermaid flowchart LR A[Typed source and document events] -- B[Atomic claims] B -- C[Probabilistic stance] C -- D[Provenance and dependence graph] D --

It does not download a model or call an external service. The built-in claim extractor and stance scorer are transparent research fixtures, not substitutes for a production NLI model. Core design Claim-conditioned trust Trust is represented as a source confusion model over support, refute, insufficient evidence, and malformed evidence. The posterior uses partial pooling across: - Global behavior - Source - Topic - Claim type - Source and topic - Source and claim type - Source, topic, claim type, and current regime Sparse scopes borrow strength from broader levels. Well-observed scopes become increasingly local. Online change detection Audited outcomes are processed by a Bayesian online change-point detector. Persistence and cooldown rules reduce noisy alarms. A detected compromise opens a new reliability regime for the affected scope. Recovery is tracked separately. Dependence correction Evidence is clustered using canonical URLs, content fingerprints, citation links, declared upstream sources, and token similarity. Fusion occurs at the cluster level before source reliability is applied. This prevents copied reports from being counted as independent corroboration. Decision policy The policy uses posterior confidence, conflict mass, effective independent support, uncertainty, and an audit budget. It can: -

documents.title: tempo-trust — ARCHITECTURE.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture TEMPO-Trust separates evidence processing, online learning, decision policy, and auditability. Each stage accepts typed records and emits a ledger event. Processing path 1. Register sources with conservative identity rules 2. Ingest a typed document 3. Extract atomic claims with topic, claim type, and valid time 4. Score each evidence and claim pair 5. Update provenance and dependence clusters 6. Fuse evidence once per independent cluster 7. Read the hierarchical reliability posterior 8. Select an answer, retrieval, audit, explanation, or abstention action 9. Record the complete decision trace 10. Apply delayed audits when they become available 11. Update trust and online change detection The prediction always precedes its audit. This ordering prevents label leakage in streaming evaluation. State boundaries The engine owns: - Source registry - Document and claim records - Evidence records - Provenance graph - Hierarchical trust state - Change-point detectors - Policy budget - Alarm history - Trust timeline The ledger remains the authoritative event history. Materialized state can be rebuilt and checked against the live state hash. Trust update Each audited evidence item contributes fractional sufficient statistics using its stance probability vector. Recent observations receive more weight through exponential decay. The full source, topic, claim type, and regime posterior is partially pooled with broader scopes. The model intentionally separates: - Source quality from source identity - Relevance from correctness - Independent support from repeated support -

documents.title: evidroute — docs/architecture.md - part 1
documents.summary: Architecture EvidRoute models evidence acquisition as a bounded sequential decision process. At every step, the router may acquire from one feasible source or stop with ANSWER, ASK USER, or ABSTAIN. ``text Query + budget + risk target + snapshot | decision features | probes + health + policy scorer | conservative utility ranking | acquire one typed evidence bundle | normalize - deduplicate - detect conflict | answer + citation + risk check | | stop acquire next route ` Components | Component | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | models.py | Strict schemas for budgets, evidence, candidates, decisions, and traces | | routes/ | Stable adapter contract and seven route implementations | | routing/policy.py | Decision-time scoring, feasibility, value of information, stop rule | | routing/learned.py | CPU potential-outcome utility model trained from forced routes | | synthesis/ | Evidence-only answer selection, deduplication, conflict policy | | risk/ | One-sided selective-risk bounds and source-shift detection | | counterfactual/ | Forced-route potential outcomes, oracle, and atomic regret | | observability/ | Local SQLite traces, feedback, canonical JSON export | | api.py | FastAPI transport, validation, upload guardrails, SSE | | apps/web | React console for decisions, evidence, conflicts, budgets, and replay | Route contract Each route exposes availability, estimate, probe, acquire, health, and close. documents.summary: used at decision time. Offline implementation BM25 is implemented from corpus statistics. Dense retrieval uses deterministic signed feature hashing, making the smoke path CPU-only and reproducible. Structured retrieval performs bounded graph traversal with source-document provenance. Frozen web uses versioned snapshots. The live web adapter is deliberately unavailable in the default configuration. Invariants 1. An answer in verified mode must cite normalized, safe evidence. 2. Every route call spends its estimate from a multidimensional budget. 3. Source failure, privacy denial, and malformed/no-result states are typed. 4. Trace export includes the configuration hash, source versions, model versions, and timing. 5. Shift detection invalidates the calibration guarantee instead of silently reusing it.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/adr/0001-offline-first.md
documents.summary: ADR 0001: Credential-free offline reference path - Status: accepted - Date: 2026-07-23 Decision The default system must run without API keys or network access. External web evidence is modeled with frozen, versioned snapshots; a live route exists only as a disabled typed adapter. Consequences Smoke tests are deterministic, inexpensive, and safe to run in CI. They do not demonstrate live web performance. A future live provider requires a new threat review, provider-specific reliability measurements, and recalibration.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/adr/0002-risk-and-shift.md
documents.summary: ADR 0002: Conservative selective risk with explicit shift invalidation - Status: accepted - Date: 2026-07-23 Decision Answer acceptance uses a one-sided Wilson upper bound on the unsupported-or-incorrect loss. Calibration metadata names the loss, confidence, sample size, threshold, snapshot, and guarantee status. Detected source or error-rate shift changes the status to unavailable under shift. Consequences The system may abstain more often than a point-estimate threshold. The bound is a transparent prototype controller, not a universal distribution-free guarantee under arbitrary dependence. Small or shifted strata require abstention, pooled fallback, or explicit recalibration.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/related-work.md - part 1
documents.summary: Related work and design synthesis EvidRoute is an original implementation inspired by research directions in the four manuscripts below. It is not an official reproduction, and no source implementation, private data, or reported experimental result from those works was copied into this repository. - Moskvoretskii et al., Adaptive Retrieval without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home (ACL 2025), motivates explicit comparison between adaptive retrieval and uncertainty estimation, including efficiency rather than answer quality alone. - Wu et al., Search Wisely (EMNLP 2025), frames over-search and under-search through uncertainty. EvidRoute therefore records stop decisions, route costs, and both missed and unnecessary acquisition behavior. - Qian and Liu, Scent of Knowledge (NeurIPS 2025), treats iterative retrieval as information foraging. EvidRoute's sequential policy uses a transparent information-value term and permits multiple evidence acquisitions. - Shi et al., τ-Knowledge (ICML 2026 manuscript), evaluates conversational agents that combine unstructured knowledge, tools, policy, and user interaction. EvidRoute includes ASK USER, privacy/policy failures, and a local-only archive adapter without redistributing private data. The distinct research question here is whether a policy can choose among heterogeneous evidence and interaction sources under an explicit risk target, source shift, and constrained budget. documents.title: evidroute — docs/reproducibility.md
documents.summary: Reproducibility The credential-free MiniRoute path is the executable reference experiment. ``bash python -m evidroute.cli reproduce-mini --output artifacts/reproduce-mini --seed 17 ` The run writes forced-route outcomes, a learned router checkpoint, calibration data, raw predictions, aggregate metrics, corruption manifests, drift results, CSV/SVG report assets, and run manifest.json`. The manifest records: - Python, platform, and relevant package versions; - random seed and validated engine configuration; - configuration SHA-256; - hashes of every bundled MiniRoute input; - Git commit and worktree status, when available; - snapshot, index, and schema versions. Determinism applies to the bundled CPU routes and MiniRoute input. Wall-clock timings, operating system scheduling, dependency solver output, and floating-point behavior across different architectures may vary. A public benchmark run is a separate experiment and must retain its license, download provenance, original split, preprocessing hash, and evaluation command. Scientific claim boundary The generated smoke report demonstrates that the pipeline executes and emits auditable artifacts. It is not evidence that EvidRoute outperforms published systems. The repository does not report a public benchmark result until the corresponding run exists.

documents.title: trace-mem — README.md - part 1
documents.summary: TRACE-Mem TRACE-Mem is an executable reliability layer for persistent AI agents. It maps how faults travel from memory writes to irreversible tool actions, finds the stages that caused a failed run, and verifies risky actions before they are committed. The included claims workflow is a complete reference implementation. A case evolves across sessions: an address changes, coverage is updated, and the preferred contact channel changes. TRACE-Mem records those facts in a bi-temporal memory, injects controlled faults at five stages, replays failures with targeted repairs, learns an interaction-aware risk model, and applies a verification gate before the final action. What is implemented - Append-only, bi-temporal memory with active, superseded, and disputed states. - Fault injection at memory write, consolidation, retrieval, reasoning, and tool-action stages. - Trace-level signals for write gaps, active-memory conflicts, stale retrievals, inconsistent reasoning, and mutated tool payloads. - Counterfactual replay that repairs one stage at a time and records whether the failed action recovers. - A causal reliability map that measures pairwise fault interaction lift. - An interaction-aware risk model learned from historical traces. - A pre-commit risk gate that verifies source events and rebuilds the proposed action when risk exceeds a configurable threshold. - An offline HTML operations dashboard plus JSON and CSV exports. documents.title: trace-mem — README.md - part 2
documents.summary: mem.py --output-dir .\results Start-Process .\results\dashboard.html ` Useful options: `powershell python .\trace mem.py --seed 7 --train-runs 5000 --test-runs 1500 --risk-threshold 0.55 ` Generated artifacts: - dashboard.html: reliability, intervention, and trace explorer - results.json: complete machine-readable run output - scenario results.csv: per-case operating metrics - reliability map.csv: pairwise causal interaction map Test `powershell python -m unittest discover -s .\tests -v `` Runtime flow 1. The agent stages a tool action instead of immediately committing it. 2. TRACE-Mem derives reliability signals from the complete memory-to-action trace. 3. The learned model estimates failure risk, including interactions between signals. 4. Low-risk actions commit normally. High-risk actions are verified against the source-event adapter, rebuilt, and then committed. 5. Failed historical traces can be replayed with targeted repairs to produce causal attributions and improve verification policy. The built-in claims cases contain generated data and serve as a reproducible local workload. The runtime classes are domain-independent: another agent can provide its own source events, staged action payload, evaluator, and verifier without changing the reliability model.
